Subject: Renewal window — EU primary & APAC rollout questions

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the partnership — our renewal is up in December and the execs want to make sure our next term covers two items before we sign:

1) Move our primary residency to the EU (data-at-rest + processing) for PHI handling.
2) Staged APAC rollout with a warm-standby failover (no hot full-time capacity initially).

We need clarity on:
- Any term changes or minimum commit required for EU primary?
- How cross-region failover will affect RUs and cost (prefix KV caching implications)?
- Evidence we can show security/compliance (SOC2 artifacts, audit logs) during the negotiation.

Alan (cc'd) is our infra lead and will flag any tech constraints. Can you share a draft SOW and a cost delta for the EU shift + APAC warm-standby? Ideally we want a single renewal that handles both.

Appreciate a concise plan — execs prefer a playbook with milestones and owners.

Best,
Sophie Lam
Director of Platform Engineering
StarkCare Health

Hi Sophie — thanks for the clear ask. High level answers up front, followed by next steps and who owns what.

Summary:
- Term: We can keep a 12-month renewal or move to a 24-month committed contract. The EU primary residency requires a modest reserved-capacity uplift (see cost note below).
- APAC: We recommend an APAC warm-standby configuration (standby nodes with burst license + cold-burst allowance) for the pilot phase — lower cost than full dedicated capacity.
- Compliance: We will provide SOC2 evidence, scoped audit logs, and a runbook for failover drills.

Immediate next steps we propose:
1) I will share a redlined SOW (attached) that includes the EU residency addendum and APAC warm-standby plan.
2) Monica (CS) will provide the technical playbook and a failover runbook for your infra team to review.
3) Ben (cc'd) will provide pricing scenarios: 12m vs 24m, and the estimated RU delta for the failover plan.

Cost delta (ballpark):
- EU primary residency: +18% on unit charge due to reserved node footprint to meet latency/residency SLOs.
- APAC warm-standby: fixed monthly standby license + per-token burst charge; expect +7–12% in total TCO for a staged rollout.

I'll attach: Redwood_SOW_v2.pdf (draft with EU addendum), and apac-warmstandby-cost-model.xlsx.

When can your team do a 30‑minute alignment session next week? I can loop in product if we need a kernel/caching deep-dive.

Thanks —

Subject: Technical playbook: EU primary + APAC warm-standby (draft)

Hi Sophie/Alan — Monica on CS ops. Sharing a concise runbook for the proposed configuration; keeping it high level here and attaching the drive link with the full playbook: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1ExampleRunbook

Key points:
- EU primary: Customer data and inference compute pinned to the EU cluster; VPC peering + KMS integration for keys. Models will run on EU-resident nodes; we recommend pinning model versions for the first 30 days after cutover.
- APAC warm-standby: A small fleet (10–15% of baseline capacity) kept warm with a license fee. Burst paths will instantiate additional nodes in APAC via autoscaling; KV/prefix cache will be primed during scheduled synchronization windows to reduce cold-start latency.
- Failover behavior:
  - Planned failover: DNS switchover + graceful cache rehydration window (approx 90s additional latency for first requests).
  - Unplanned failover: Traffic routes to APAC standby only if EU capacity is degraded; for strict sovereignty scenarios we can restrict what fails over (metadata-only vs full payload).

Operational items we need from you:
- A list of endpoints that must remain EU-only (PHI endpoints).
- Preferred 48-hour maintenance window for cache priming prior to cutover.
- SLA expectations during pilot (we propose a 24-hour rollback window for the first month).

Security/compliance:
- SOC2 artifacts and audit log slices can be shared under an NDA. I've included SOC2-evidence-refs.zip with index pointers.

I'll be on the alignment call to walk the runbook.

—Monica
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.ai

- Option B (24m committed, preferred for discounts): +12% MRC + one-time migration credit equal to 1 month of baseline usage.

If you want to lock EU residency without a long-term commit, we can do a 3‑month reserved uplift with clear rollback terms — that reduces initial spend but we would need a short-term scheduling window for the migration.
